result.title: SARATHI: Decoupled Data-Free Probing and Adaptive Reconstruction for Structured LLM Pruning
result.summary: Structured pruning reduces the inference cost of large language models (LLMs) by permanently removing neurons and weight rows, yielding dense, hardware-agnostic speedup. Existing post-training methods couple neuron selection and weight reconstruction through a shared calibration dataset, introducing domain bias and out-of-memory failures at high sparsity. We propose SARATHI, a framework that decouples these two stages. A data-free \emph{NMF Residual Subspace Probe} scores neurons using intrinsic weight geometry, without accessing any calibration data, and carries a formal connection to Robust PCA. \emph{Adaptive OBS} then reconstructs the pruned weights with a localized calibration batch, operating in $\mathcal{O}(d^2)$ peak memory per layer and eliminating the global memory bottleneck of coupled methods. A \emph{Bias Shift Compensation} step corrects systematic activation drift in post-LayerNorm architectures that would otherwise cause perplexity collapse at high sparsity. Experiments across six models from two architecture families (gated and non-gated FFN) at 15--40\% sparsity show that SARATHI achieves competitive perplexity and matches or exceeds existing structured pruning baselines on zero-shot accuracy.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 SARATHI，将结构化剪枝的神经元选择与权重重建解耦：用无需校准数据的 NMF 残差子空间探针按权重内在几何打分，再用局部校准的 Adaptive OBS 在 O(d²) 峰值内存下重建权重，并加入偏置漂移补偿以缓解高稀疏下的困惑度崩溃。
AI.relevance_reason: 其无数据的子空间重要性评分与 OBS 式的逐层贡献分配，可能为 LVR 中判别内部 latent 状态哪些子空间承载视觉信息、以及特征对答案的贡献分配提供可核查的分析工具；但论文本身面向纯文本 LLM 压缩，与 VLM 推理无直接关联。
